### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getBookTree (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getBookTree, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree), meta.getBookTree (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree, selected by route anchor /book/:name/tree))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItems (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (symbol, a top-level function), /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-objectstack.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via /book/:name/tree (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via /book/:name/tree (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via /book/:name/tree (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via /book/:name/tree (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItems — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `65fd034ff3777d5d6f357cea1ddfcdde65f6f5b1` — the merge of head `c1aaf1cee64e259ab228c6a69d83df4f7d35ddc7` into base `33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 65fd034ff3777d5d6f357cea1ddfcdde65f6f5b1 && git checkout 65fd034ff3777d5d6f357cea1ddfcdde65f6f5b1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 c1aaf1cee64e259ab228c6a69d83df4f7d35ddc7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 && git merge --no-ff c1aaf1cee64e259ab228c6a69d83df4f7d35ddc7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c1aaf1cee64e259ab228c6a69d83df4f7d35ddc7`
Local-runs: none

Face: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone (no published schema, no governed path, no narrowing in the diff), reviewed by the lane seat as the declaration face asks.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: one new public method, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.readFormRequest<T>(read: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>`, reachable from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s `.` entry (`src/index.ts:3` exports the class). Right as a widening: additive, optional to call, and the one consumer (`packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`) feature-detects it (`typeof p.readFormRequest === 'function'`), so a protocol without it serves exactly as before.
- Accept set: unchanged. Every answer of `getMetaItems`, `getMetaItemsPerPackage` and `getUnreadableFormBodies` is the same items in the same order; only the number of underlying reads changes. The 11 existing form-door files (898 cases, asserting answers) are green, and the new pin asserts exact read counts with two CONTROLs.
- New exports from `protocol-form-reads.ts` (`readInFormRequest`, `formRequestScope`, `inFormRequestScope`): module-internal, not re-exported from `src/index.ts` — not published surface.
- Runtime dependency: `node:async_hooks` in an already node-only package (`check:lean-entry-closure` green on this head).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `@objectstack/rest` patch, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right by AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 (the level follows the metadata-protocol kind; `none` ships patch) and `check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis; Check Changeset `success` on this head. The `Clause-②` line is identical in the changeset and the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, `form-routes.ts` outside the claimed surface: the measured producer of the door's repeated reads (five protocol calls); accepted, recorded in the seat's claim amendment 7234355369.
- Dev flag, one pass-through row in `rest-write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts`'s READS table: no assertion changed; accepted.
- Scope lifetime: the memo is per `readInFormRequest` call (`AsyncLocalStorage`), closed in `finally`; outside a reading it is the one call's own; a continuation after the request reads the store directly. No cross-request cache (that stays `meta-overlay-cache.ts`). Memo keys carry `type`, `packageId`, `names`, `previewDrafts`, `audience`, `layer` (lists) and `type`, `packageId` (rows): no key collapses two different reads.
- Shared results: the module copies before it writes (`projectedServed` spreads the item; the other writes are to local arrays; the one sort is on a copy), so a memoized row set or list is not mutated by a later reader in the same request.
- SQL push-down: no finding — the change removes repeated reads; no id materialisation or in-app join is added.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37709-form-reads-once`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSAaBEfQpU2yJexSJ8`

**VERDICT: PASS**
